newsitem.title: eritrea: Sudan rebels say Khartoum receiving Iraqi arms.
newsitem.headline: Sudan rebels say Khartoum receiving Iraqi arms.

text.p: The Sudanese opposition's rebel commander said on Friday a ship loaded with Iraqi weapons from a storage in Yemen arrived in Port Sudan for the government last week.
"From our sources in Port Sudan, we hear a ship by the name of al-Obied, commanded by Captain Naji Asam Maki, came from Mukalla (in Yemen) taking arms to Sudan," General Fathi Ahmed Ali.
He told Reuters that his source was working within the military command of Port Sudan.
There was no independent confirmation of the accusation and no immediate comment from Sudan's government, Yemen or Iraq.

"When they were offloading the ship, a bomb exploded and killed Colonel Abu Alama al-Bakhid Hassan and lightly injured Major General Abbas al-Sayeed, who is the area commander of Port Sudan," he said.
"It was reported in Khartoum that the officer was killed during routine testing of weapons."
The opposition's military commander said Sudanese President Lieutenant-General Omar Hassan al-Bashir travelled to Port Sudan on the day of the blast, which was February 20.
He said the arms included 600 anti-tank weapons and were just a part of the Iraqi weapons being stored in Yemen.
Ali heads the military wing of the National Democratic Alliance, a coalition of opposition groups based in Asmara.
